Research News! Announcing the 1st release of fundamental AI research from the Open-Endedness Team @LilaSciences: a vision-focused blog + 4 preprints. The blog details a broad research agenda for achieving open-endedness while each paper unveils its own novel research direction.

The ideas covered in the papers include:

• a novel approach to training for creativity designed to sidestep a newly-identified problem called the “creative paradox,” which means that directly reinforcing creative outputs can sometimes limit reaching full creative potential;

• an investigation of the advantages of seeing the world through fresh eyes by training an LLM that is intentionally naïve in a certain area (in effect presenting less data as a potential advantage);

• a new kind of training regularization technique for SGD called unified factored organizers (UFOs), which is designed to achieve unified factored representation (UFR) as seen in Picbreeder CPPNs;

• and finally a unique study of catastrophic forgetting that shows that networks with UFR (like those from Picbreeder) are intrinsically resistant to catastrophic forgetting. The inset video on this post is a visualization from that catastrophic forgetting work.

The blog post also includes an interactive “wheel of science” demo.

The implications of these ideas are broad and diverse, but the fun part is that each one opens up its own new research playground - there is a lot of room for further research here!

Moreover, we hope this release also highlights one other important point about AI today: while it may seem that the road ahead is already paved and all that’s left is to drive mindlessly forward, there actually remains a lot of room for new directions and insights in the pursuit of open-endedness and creativity.

This research was possible because @LilaSciences appreciates the critical role of open-ended innovation in the pursuit of scientific superintelligence. The advances you see here are part of this much larger company-wide ambition, which includes AI Science Factories and many other unprecedented components. When this engine is fueled by open-endedness, the result will be much more than a step change.

More advances in open-endedness are coming!
